question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the cotangent-cosecant identity 

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡x-1={cot}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic identity

$$
{coth}^{2}⁡x-{csch}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{7}\frac{{coth}^{4}⁡x-{csch}^{2}⁡x\,{coth}^{2}⁡x}{{coth}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{2}^{7}\frac{{coth}^{2}⁡x({coth}^{2}⁡x-{csch}^{2}⁡x)}{{coth}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{7}({coth}^{2}⁡x-{csch}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{7}\text{d}x \\  & =x{|}_{2}^{7} \\  & =7-2 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$
